question: The Albufera de Valencia Natural Park is a wetland of international importance (Ramsar site), included in the Natura 2000 Network and with numerous approved LIFE projects. The European Green Deal includes the EU Biodiversity Strategy. The Nature Restoration Regulation lays down a requirement to avoid deterioration and requires states to take measures to prevent damage to Natura 2000 sites.

The current expansion of the port of Valencia lacks an environmental impact assessment, a situation that has been repeatedly denounced to the European institutions, and the Commission must therefore act in accordance with the European Green Deal.
We believe that the negative impacts of the expansion of the port of Valencia are weighing less heavily than the profits to be made by the Swiss multinational that is promoting the expansion. 1.

Does the Commission consider that the expansion to the north of the port of Valencia should receive European funding, given that an environmental impact assessment has not been carried out and the project affects an area included in the Natura 2000 network?
Is the Commission aware that funds have been requested for this infrastructure project and others directly associated with it?
Does the Commission intend to remind the Spanish Government of its duty not to allow damage to occur to the Albufera de Valencia Natural Park?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.3.2024) As the Commission stated in its reply to written question E-003263/2021, the competent national authorities must decide, under the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Directive1, whether a new environmental impact assessment is necessary for the proposed extension of Port of Valencia.

Under the Habitats Directive2, before agreeing to a project which is likely to have a significant effect on a Natura 2000 site, the competent authorities must appropriately assess and confirm that there will be no implications for the site3,4. The EIA provides for specific review procedures to challenge the substantive or procedural legality of the decision, or the lack thereof, made by the competent authority.

In the 2021-2027 programming period, the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) is planned to support the improvement of the access of ports by rail, to increase the modal connectivity under the National Multi-regional Operational Programme. Thus, the extension of the Port of Valencia as such has not been financed by the ERDF or the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF).

However, an on-going project co-funded under CEF1-Transport5 aims at enhancing the rail connection to the port. The Cohesion Policy and CEF funds are awarded in line with the EU acquis and, particularly, in accordance with the environmental legislation in force. Projects that may significantly affect the environment must comply with the applicable provisions of EU environmental law6.

The Spanish Recovery and Resilience Plan7 also includes projects related to the accessibility and sustainability of the Port of Valencia. The milestones and targets included in this investment will be assessed in the fourth8, seventh and tenth payment requests. 1 Directive 2011/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on the assessment

of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment Text with EEA relevance - OJ L 26, 28.1.2012, p. 1–21, as amended by Directive 2014/52/EU of 16 April 2014 - OJ L 124, 25.4.2014, p. 1–18 (EIA Directive). 2 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7–50.

3 Member States may establish coordinated and/or joint procedures when the obligation to carry out assessments arises simultaneously from both Directives. See Commission guidance document on streamlining environmental assessments conducted under Article 2(3) of the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive (2016/C 273/01). 4 Without prejudice of Article 6(4) of the Habitats Directive. 5 Please see https://ec.europa.

7–25; and Directive 2000/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2000 establishing a framework for Community action in the field of water policy - OJ L 327, 22.12.2000, p. 1–73. 7 under the investment 3 of component 6 (C6.I3). 8 Currently being under review.
At this stage, the Commission is not aware of projects directly associated with the expansion to the north of the port of Valencia.
